q: Most musical instruments produce sound due to vibration of the string and air column.
e: True. Most musical instruments produce sound due to vibration of the string and air column. Most instruments make sound from a vibrating string or a vibrating air column.

q: Most musical instruments produce sound due to vibration of the solid body only.
e: False. The claim puts solid where string belongs. Most musical instruments produce sound due to vibration of the string and air column. Musical instruments speak from vibrating strings and air columns, not from a solid body alone.

q: These vibrations give rise to waves known as stationary waves in the string or air column.

q: These vibrations give rise to waves known as progressive waves in the string or air column.

q: Waves are classified as progressive waves and stationary waves.
e: True. Waves are classified as progressive waves and stationary waves. Waves are either progressive, travelling out, or stationary, staying put.

q: Progressive waves spread out from the region in which they are produced.
e: True. Progressive waves spread out from the region in which they are produced. Progressive waves leave the source. Stationary waves do not spread out.

q: Stationary waves spread out from the region in which they are produced.

q: Stationary waves are also called standing waves.

q: Sound waves which travel in air when we speak are progressive waves.
e: True. Sound waves which travel in air when we speak are progressive waves. Speech in air is a progressive wave, not a standing wave.

q: Water waves which travel on the water surface when a stone is dropped are stationary waves.
e: False. Ripples from a stone are progressive waves on the surface.

q: Progressive waves carry energy through the medium.
e: True. Progressive waves carry energy through the medium. A progressive wave carries energy through the medium.
